clue.text: Those responsible for 5 4 draw goose eggs in the modern fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the six words before it are reshaped into new names

explanation.surface: Writers of a famous book are told to sketch goose eggs in a contemporary style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like a noun after 'modern' but is a verb, the anagram signal for the six words before it. The brothers wrote The Diary of a Nobody (1892), Weedon also drawing its pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian comic novel The Diary of a Nobody was written by these two brothers together.

clue.text: We are inclined to write "Dear Sir" and argue

definitions.text: We are inclined to write "Dear Sir" and argue

indicators.note: being inclined to write the words differently, the letters of these three words are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Readers of a newspaper admit their habit of firing off argumentative letters to the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DEAR SIR, AND and ARGUE are rearranged; the whole clue also describes this paper's readers, who write in to argue with the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-portrait of a newspaper's audience, who are famous for sending argumentative letters beginning with that salutation.

clue.text: I leave French deity among worthies in Roman theatre

indicators.note: among says one group of letters sits inside the other

parts.note: OM, the Order of Merit, is an honour held by distinguished people, worthies

indicators.note: I leave means the letter I goes out of the French word

parts.note: Dieu is French for God

explanation.surface: A god of the French departs from a gathering of great men in an ancient playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeum was a roofed building in ancient Rome used for music and recitals, a kind of small theatre.

clue.text: Collector of string less bulky?

parts.note: G is one of the strings of a violin or guitar, named by its note
leaner means slimmer, less bulky

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a collector of string is thinner than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collector of string' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Collector'; 'string' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner gathers leftover grain from the field after harvest, a collector of scraps.

clue.text: See 5
Young and old beginners in climbing scared over their getting involved with Bond in the record book

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the first piece above the second
in places one set of letters within the other
in a down entry, climbing reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: scared means afraid

indicators.note: beginners means the first letters of the words named
getting involved with stirs the letters of these pieces together into a new order

parts.note: their points back to those same beginners of young and old, Y and O

explanation.surface: Young and old novices, frightened while climbing, end up tangled with a secret agent in a logbook.
explanation.walkthrough: AFRAID read upwards is DIARFA; Y and O go into it to make DIARYOFA. 'their' reuses Y and O, which 'getting involved with' mixes into BOND to give NOBODY.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary is a daily record, and this famous comic novel takes the form of one, so it is a record book.

clue.text: … but now pretty? Elucidate

definitions.meaning: someone formerly plain but now pretty is an ... person, read as a joke compound
to elucidate is to make clear, to account for

explanation.definitionFit: Elucidating something means making it clear; the joke sense is someone no longer plain-looking.

clue.text: Hell for man around frequently with a cuppa in the old days

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, Hell

indicators.note: around puts the first piece on both sides of the second

parts.note: he stands for a man
oft is an old word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: A man condemned to hell keeps turning up with a cup of tea, as people did long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of tea was the eighteenth-century way of saying a cup of tea, an old-fashioned cuppa.

clue.text: Some notification for new unfinished hell — hell? Over my dead body!

indicators.note: some says only part of the word that follows is used, its opening stretch
unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the pit is a name for hell

explanation.surface: A frantic notice about hell, written in a hurry, ends in a furious refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes NOTIFICA from 'notification'; 'unfinished' cuts 'hell' to HEL, and the second 'hell' is PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic refusals: an exclamation meaning you will stop it from happening if at all possible.

clue.text: Acuity in 27 called for a knife or a lawyers' profit

indicators.note: called means spoken out, so these words are heard as something else

parts.note: said quickly, these words sound like a phrase meaning a keen sight for something
the Bar is the body of barristers, lawyers
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Sharp business sense is likened to a blade, or to what barristers make.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is TRADE, so the definition is sharpness in business. Spoken aloud, 'a knife or a' sounds like the first four words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a keen nose for a good deal is exactly acuity in trade, the shrewd shopper's gift.

clue.text: Assume one should be clad in mail

indicators.note: clad in means dressed in, so the one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: post is mail
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone presumes a knight ought to be dressed in chain mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mail' suggests armour, but here it is the letters you send: POST.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to assume or put forward as a basis for argument.

clue.text: Tenor note in spotted tile

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a domino is a tile marked with spots
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A singer's note rings out among dotted pieces in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Plácido Domingo is a celebrated Spanish operatic tenor, an example of the voice type.

clue.text: Sabbatical return of r-raid without quarter

indicators.note: return of says the whole assembly is read backwards
without here means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: the stammered r-raid suggests a stammered f-foray, a foray being a raid
E, east, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A stuttering raider takes a break, coming home without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without quarter' sounds like 'giving no mercy', but 'without' means outside: the stutter F-FORAY goes round E, and 'return of' reads FFORAEY backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabbatical is a year away from normal work, a year's leave.

clue.text: 2 to say "Are you in debt?"

indicators.note: to say means the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: the question is d'you owe? in casual speech

explanation.surface: A pair asks whether the other owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, "D'you owe?" (are you in debt?) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair, two of something.

clue.text: Ancient cross featuring heavenly being's shortened lines

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an angel is a heavenly being
Rly is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: An old cross shows an angel's lines cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like a crucifix, but it means angry; the answer is an archaic form of 'angrily'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for angry or angrily, so 'ancient' tells you it is archaic and 'cross' gives the sense.

clue.text: See 1 across
Head off a French colour current in the Balkans

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: bleu is French for blue

explanation.surface: A French flag colour loses its top in the Balkan current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' is not a stream here but currency, money that is current.
explanation.definitionFit: The leu is the currency of Romania and Moldova, Balkan money.

clue.text: I'm tremendously keen to dissipate fat and I can!

indicators.note: dissipating fat scatters it, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An enthusiast vows that they can burn off the fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic is a person with extreme, obsessive enthusiasm for something.

clue.text: Tail off a horse in personal memoranda

indicators.note: tail off means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: Notes in a diary about cutting a horse's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Ana are collected anecdotes or sayings of a person, their personal memorabilia.

clue.text: Royal Society eating hat? Not quite, just a lozenge

indicators.note: eating means one piece swallows the other
not quite means the word is cut short at the end

parts.note: a homburg is a felt hat

explanation.surface: Scientists eating a hat just get a throat sweet instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lozenge' suggests a cough sweet; here it is the diamond shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a four-sided figure with equal sides, a lozenge or diamond shape.

clue.text: Inlet by the sea? That's a horse of another colour

parts.note: a bay is an inlet of the coast
mare is Latin for sea

explanation.surface: An inlet by the sea is said to be another thing altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a horse of another colour' is an idiom for a different matter, but here it is literal: a female horse of reddish-brown colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay mare is a female horse with a reddish-brown coat, literally a horse of a colour.

clue.text: Scots out in island in Malaysia

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands
awa is Scots for away, out

explanation.surface: Scotsmen are away on an island in Malaysia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarawak is a state of Malaysia on the island of Borneo, so it lies within that country.

clue.text: See 9
Ringer at home to one composer and three painters

parts.note: a bell rings, so it is a ringer
in means at home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer at home plays host to a musician and three artists.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincenzo Bellini wrote operas, and Jacopo, Gentile and Giovanni Bellini were Venetian painters.

clue.text: Give food and drink to judge concerned with call for silence

parts.note: a ref, referee, judges a game
re means about, concerned with
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: A judge is fed and watered while calling for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh someone is to revive them with food and drink.

clue.text: Champion half of 13

definitions.meaning: an expert or star performer is a champion
13 across is a pair, two, and half of two is one, the single spot on a card or die

explanation.definitionFit: A star player is called an ace, and the ace is the one-spot card, half of two.

clue.text: I prove the fool a philosopher

parts.note: an ass is a fool
A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A man declares that he shows the fool to be a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prove' is in the metallurgist's sense, to test the quality of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An assayer tests or proves the purity of metals, so the definition is the speaker describing his job.

clue.text: Well found in comparatively modern chateau

indicators.note: found in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: late means recent, comparatively modern
fit means healthy, well

explanation.surface: A spring is discovered in a fairly new French castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' suggests water, but it means healthy: FIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Château Lafite is a famous Bordeaux wine estate, a chateau; older spellings double the T.

clue.text: Deal with wind

definitions.meaning: to deal is to buy and sell, do business
a ... wind is a steady wind of the tropics

explanation.definitionFit: Trading is dealing, and the trade wind blows steadily towards the equator.

clue.text: Heather, I call some of it

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone names a sprig of heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to heather: the answer is the botanical name for heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, so it names the plant the clue opens with.

clue.text: A little cheese, a quiet menace in a coal mine

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount
Edam is a Dutch cheese
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: A scrap of cheese and a hush prove a danger underground.
explanation.definitionFit: White damp is carbon monoxide in mines, a poisonous gas and so a danger to miners.

clue.text: Click — there's Hick out — horror!

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A click sounds, a country bumpkin is ejected, and there is terror.
explanation.definitionFit: German for frightfulness, used for deliberate terrorising of civilians in wartime, hence horror.
